newsitem.title: CANADA: Mineral Resources withdraws from zinc spat.
newsitem.headline: Mineral Resources withdraws from zinc spat.

text.p: Mineral Resources Corp said on Monday it will not stand in the way of Anvil Range Mining Corp's plan for a private placement of 4.1 million common shares with Cominco Ltd.
"We've got to take the high ground," Mineral Resources chairman Cliff Frame said in a phone interview.

Frame returned last week from a trip to South Korea in an attempt to pursuade Hyundai Corp, currently Anvil's largest shareholder, to oppose the private placement with Cominco. But Hyundai decided to support the private placement, Frame said.

Mineral Resources said last month it was planning a share-based takeover bid for Anvil Range, whose main asset is the Faro zinc and lead mine in Canada's Yukon. Mining at Faro ceased in December after Anvil ran into lower metal grades and higher operating costs.
When Anvil Range said it planned a private placement with Cominco, effectively sidelining the Mineral Resources takeover plan, Frame asked the Toronto Stock Exchange to require a shareholder vote.
But without Hyundai on side, the vote would be academic, Frame said Monday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange ended its inquiry into the ransaction on Monday, said Ralph Shay, the TSE's vice-president of company listings and regulation.
Other companies have also shown interest in bidding for Anvil Range, but the Cominco plan has squeezed them out, Frame said.
"It's the worst deal you could ever imagine" for Anvil Range shareholders, Frame said.
After the share issue, Cominco will own 28 percent of Anvil. Hyundai's share will be diluted to 20 percent from 25 percent.
While Mineral Resources would not stand in the way of the Cominco transaction, the company would watch closely, Frame said.
"We'll just have to watch it for a while. It's not over until it's over."
Cominco said on Monday it had until February 5 to complete its review of Anvil Range to close the share transaction.

The company would be prepared to plow more cash into Anvil Range to help start up Faro again, but Cominco had no intention of taking a controlling stake in Anvil, Cominco chief executive David Thompson told a conference in Scottsdale, Arizona on Monday.
"We are not interested in taking control," he said. "We think the mine has the possibility to make good earnings but at obviously higher zinc prices."
